main.title: Fall Guys
main.summary: Fall Guys launched in August 2020 as a paid party battle royale, before becoming free-to-play in June 2022.

cards.heading: A paid launch, then Free for All
cards.text: Fall Guys launched as the paid platform battle royale game Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout on August 4, 2020, developed by Mediatonic and published by Devolver Digital for PlayStation 4 and Windows. It was also available to PlayStation Plus subscribers at launch. It was acquired by Epic Games and subsequently made free-to-play on 21 June 2022 and released on additional platforms including Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S, with full cross-platform play support among all platforms. As part of the transition, the game adopted a paid battle pass system for its monetisation. On 16 August 2024, the game was released on mobile via the Epic Games Store, worldwide on Android and only in the European Union on iOS.

cards.heading: An obstacle course for sixty beans at launch
cards.text: At launch, the main show involved up to 60 players; later versions reduced its standard player count, including a 32-player format. Players control bean-shaped characters and compete against each other in a series of randomly selected mini-games, such as obstacle courses and survival challenges. Players are eliminated as the rounds progress until, eventually, the last remaining player or team is crowned the winner. There are also many other modes, such as Explore, with different game rules and player counts. The game draws inspiration from game shows like Takeshi's Castle, It's a Knockout, Total Wipeout, and playground games like tag and British Bulldog.

cards.heading: A colourful multiplayer success
cards.text: Fall Guys received generally positive reviews from critics for its chaotic gameplay and visual appearance. The game was a commercial success, selling more than 10 million copies and attracting more than 50 million players after the game went free-to-play.

main.title: Factorio
main.subtitle: A factory from the ground up
main.summary: Factorio is Wube Software's factory-building game, whose version 1.0 arrived in August 2020 after years of public development. An engineer begins on an unfamiliar planet by gathering resources and crafting basic equipment. Furnaces, drills, belts and inserters gradually take over that work. Each new production chain supplies parts for more advanced machines and research. The factory grows through the player's decisions about where materials come from, how they travel and which tasks should become automatic next. Cooperative play lets several engineers share the construction.

cards.heading: A factory from the ground up
cards.text: Factorio is Wube Software's factory-building game, whose version 1.0 arrived in August 2020 after years of public development. An engineer begins on an unfamiliar planet by gathering resources and crafting basic equipment. Furnaces, drills, belts and inserters gradually take over that work. Each new production chain supplies parts for more advanced machines and research. The factory grows through the player's decisions about where materials come from, how they travel and which tasks should become automatic next. Cooperative play lets several engineers share the construction.

cards.heading: Following the bottleneck
cards.text: A stopped machine often points to a problem elsewhere. Iron plates may be arriving too slowly, a belt may be full or an assembly line may be consuming components faster than another can make them. Watching materials move provides the information needed to repair the system. Adding a furnace helps only when enough ore and power reach it. Expansion becomes a series of connected decisions, with a change at one end of the factory altering the needs of the rest.

cards.heading: A network to defend
cards.text: Research unlocks more ways to move resources, generate electricity and organise construction. Railways connect distant deposits, while robots can handle tasks beyond the first hand-built lines. Growing industry also creates pollution and attracts attacks from the planet's creatures. Defences must therefore share materials and power with production. The player continually balances expansion against the infrastructure supporting it. Mods and the map editor extend the same interest in systems, allowing new scenarios or substantial changes to the factory's rules.

main.title: Raji: An Ancient Epic
main.subtitle: Keeping the story alive long enough to make it
main.summary: For the team behind Raji, building a game rooted in Indian visual traditions also meant finding a way to sustain a small studio.

cards.heading: An ambitious world begins in Pune
cards.text: An ambitious visual world still needs a team that can afford to finish it. In Pune, Nodding Heads Games began developing Raji: An Ancient Epic with Indian and Balinese mythology and architecture among its references. Co-founders Shruti Ghosh, Avichal Singh and Ian Maude wanted to bring that setting to an international audience.

cards.heading: Finding a way to keep going
cards.text: The route was difficult. A crowdfunding campaign failed, and continuing the project required personal sacrifices. An Unreal Dev Grant helped the studio survive until it secured a publisher. The finished 2020 game is therefore also the record of a production that had to change its plans and keep finding the resources to continue.

cards.heading: Research becomes movement and space
cards.text: The creative decisions were specific. Research in Rajasthan informed the environments, while the heroine's background as an acrobat helped the team rethink movement and combat. Walls and pillars could become active parts of a fight rather than scenery behind it. A visual tradition had to become a place that worked under a player's control.

cards.heading: One production within a wider history
cards.text: Raji brought this team?s interpretation of Indian and Balinese influences to players internationally. Completing it required research, movement tests and changes to the production plan as funding became available. It forms one contribution to the wider history of game development in India.

main.title: Microsoft Flight Simulator
main.summary: Microsoft Flight Simulator is a 2020 flight simulation video game developed by Asobo Studio and published by Xbox Game Studios.

cards.heading: The return of Flight Simulator
cards.text: Microsoft Flight Simulator is a 2020 flight simulation video game developed by Asobo Studio and published by Xbox Game Studios. It is a sequel to Microsoft Flight Simulator X (2006) and a reboot of the Microsoft Flight Simulator series, which began in 1982. The game's development began six years prior to its release. It was released on August 18, 2020 for Windows, with a virtual reality (VR) version released in December of the same year as part of a free update. Microsoft Flight Simulator is the first installment in the series to see a VR and console release, being released on the Xbox Series X and Series S on July 27, 2021.

cards.heading: Reconstructing Earth through data
cards.text: Flight Simulator simulates the topography of the Earth using data from Bing Maps. Microsoft Azure's artificial intelligence (AI) generates the three-dimensional representations of Earth's features, using its cloud computing to render and enhance visuals, and real-world data to generate real-time weather and effects. Flight Simulator features a physics engine to provide realistic flight control surfaces, with over 1,000 simulated surfaces, as well as realistic wind modeled over hills and mountains. Some places are handcrafted, introduced in region-specific updates. To augment its realism, Azure incorporates real-time elements like natural weather and real-world air traffic.

cards.heading: Reception and a new successor
cards.text: Flight Simulator was released to critical acclaim, with universal praise for its visuals and realism, and it was cited by critics as the "safest way to travel" during the COVID-19 pandemic. Several reviewers placed it on their favorites' lists and called it the most aesthetically pleasing game of 2020, though there was some criticism of its slow loading times, inaccuracies in rendering certain buildings, and unrealistic aerodynamics models. It has been considered one of the greatest video games and it received several accolades, most notably winning "Best Sim/Strategy Game" at The Game Awards 2020, and "Strategy/Simulation Game of the Year" at the 24th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards. A sequel, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, was released in November 2024.

main.title: Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 1 + 2
main.summary: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2 is a 2020 skateboarding video game developed by Vicarious Visions and published by Activision.

cards.heading: Two skateboarding games rebuilt
cards.text: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2 is a 2020 skateboarding video game developed by Vicarious Visions and published by Activision. It was released for PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One on September 4, 2020, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on March 26, 2021, and Nintendo Switch on June 25 of the same year. It is a remake of the first two games in the Tony Hawk's series: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater (1999) and Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 (2000), which were originally developed by Neversoft. It was the first major console game in the series since Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 5 (2015) and is Vicarious Visions' final work as a subsidiary of Activision before its move under Blizzard Entertainment was announced on January 22, 2021.

cards.heading: Reception and a later successor
cards.text: The game received very positive reviews from critics who praised the graphics, diverse roster, nostalgic soundtrack, and gameplay, though some criticized the multiplayer mode and limited number of levels. The game became the fastest-selling game in the franchise, selling one million copies within the first two weeks. A successor, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 + 4, was released on July 11, 2025 and was developed by Iron Galaxy.

main.title: Hades
main.summary: Hades is a 2020 roguelike action role-playing game developed and published by Supergiant Games.

cards.heading: From Early Access to the full release
cards.text: Hades is a 2020 roguelike action role-playing game developed and published by Supergiant Games. It was released for macOS, Nintendo Switch, and Windows on September 17, 2020, following an early access release in December 2018. It was later released for PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S in August 2021, and was released for iOS in March 2024 through Netflix Games.

cards.heading: Repeated escapes and permanent improvements
cards.text: Players control Zagreus, the son of Hades, in his many attempts to escape from the Underworld and find his mother, Persephone. Aided by boons the Olympians bestow on him, he battles through a random series of rooms populated with enemies and bosses at the end of each section. The game features a hack and slash combat system; the player uses a combination of a main weapon attack, a special attack, a dash ability, and a magic ability to defeat enemies while avoiding damage to progress as far as possible. While Zagreus will often die, he can use the treasure gained during these failed runs to improve certain attributes or unlock new weapons and abilities to increase the chance of escaping on subsequent runs.

cards.heading: A roguelike structure for branching stories
cards.text: Hades was developed following Supergiant's Pyre, in which they wanted to explore procedural narrative storytelling. However, due to the nature of the gameplay, they found that players did not play through it multiple times to explore this. The roguelike structure of Hades allowed them to tell these branching stories to the player over the course of multiple playthroughs.

cards.heading: Recognition and Hades II
cards.text: Hades has been cited among the greatest video games of all time, with critics praising its narrative, gameplay, art style, music, and voice acting. It sold more than one million copies and was named game of the year by several award ceremonies and media publications. A sequel, Hades II, was released in early access in 2024, and had its full release in 2025.

main.title: Super Mario 3D All-Stars
main.summary: Super Mario 3D All-Stars is a 2020 platform game compilation developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo Switch.

cards.heading: Three adventures for the thirty-fifth anniversary
cards.text: Super Mario 3D All-Stars is a 2020 platform game compilation developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo Switch. It commemorates the 35th anniversary of Nintendo's Super Mario series, with ports of Super Mario 64 (1996), Super Mario Sunshine (2002), and Super Mario Galaxy (2007) in high-definition.

cards.heading: A compilation with a limited release window
cards.text: The compilation was released on September 18, 2020, and was available until March 31, 2021, when it was discontinued and removed from the Nintendo eShop. It received positive reviews for its games, technical improvements, and controls, but was criticized for its presentation, lack of additional content, time-limited release, and the absence of Super Mario Galaxy 2 (2010). As of March 2021, Super Mario 3D All-Stars had shipped more than 9 million copies worldwide, making it one of the best-selling video games of 2020.

main.title: Art of Rally
main.summary: Art of Rally (stylized as art of rally) is a racing video game developed and published by Funselektor Labs.

cards.heading: An alternative golden era of rally
cards.text: Art of Rally (stylized as art of rally) is a racing video game developed and published by Funselektor Labs. The game was released on September 23, 2020 for Windows, macOS, and Linux; on August 12, 2021 for Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch; on October 6, 2021 for PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5; and mobile ports published by Noodlecake were released for iOS on January 18, 2024 and Android on March 26, 2024. Art of Rally is set during the golden era of rally, in an alternate timeline where Group B was never discontinued. Players compete in rallies, unlocking classes and cars as they progress through the game.

cards.heading: Reception across different platforms
cards.text: Art of Rally received generally favorable reviews for Windows and Xbox, while the Switch version received mixed reviews.

main.title: Genshin Impact
main.summary: Genshin Impact is miHoYo?s 2020 free-to-play action RPG, combining an open world with elemental combat and a party of interchangeable characters.

cards.heading: An open world of elements and characters
cards.text: Genshin Impact is a 2020 action role-playing game developed and published by miHoYo. Its open-world exploration uses anime-inspired visuals and a battle system combining elemental magic with character switching. The free-to-play game funds regular updates through gacha purchases and is distributed internationally under the HoYoverse name. It first appeared on Android, iOS, PlayStation 4 and Windows, with further versions following.

cards.heading: The journey across Teyvat
cards.text: Genshin Impact takes inspiration from a variety of sources, including the game The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, anime, Gnosticism, and an array of real-world cultures and mythologies. The game takes place in the fantasy world of Teyvat, home to seven nations each tied to a different element and ruled by individual gods called "Archons". The story follows the Traveler, an interstellar adventurer who is separated from their twin sibling after the two land in Teyvat. Together with their guide Paimon, the Traveler journeys across the nations of Teyvat in search of their lost sibling. Along the way, the two make friends with Teyvat's people, become involved in the affairs of its nations, and unravel the mysteries of the land.

cards.heading: Reception, debates and commercial results
cards.text: Genshin Impact has received generally positive reviews, with critics praising its combat mechanics and open-world system, but some criticism has been directed at its endgame and its monetization model. The game has also been involved in controversies over censorship of content related to Chinese politics, as well as privacy and security concerns. The game performed very well commercially; at its fourth anniversary in 2024, PocketGamer.biz reported AppMagic estimates of US$6.3 billion in gross revenue on the App Store and Google Play, not total revenue across all platforms. It has received several awards, including Best Mobile Game at the Game Awards 2021 and Still Playing Award at the 2023 Golden Joystick Awards.

main.title: Super Mario Bros. 35
main.subtitle: Thirty-five players return to familiar courses
main.summary: Super Mario Bros. 35 turns courses from the 1985 game into a thirty-five-player contest where defeated enemies are sent to opponents.

cards.heading: A thirty-five-player anniversary game
cards.text: Super Mario Bros. 35 was Nintendo?s online anniversary game for Switch, released on October 1, 2020. Thirty-five players tackled courses from the 1985 original at the same time. Defeated enemies were sent to opponents, and earning more time helped keep a run going. The service was available to Nintendo Switch Online members until March 31, 2021.

cards.heading: Sending enemies to opponents
cards.text: Defeating an enemy clears a path and sends another obstacle to a rival. Players choose targets while watching their own course, using familiar enemies to put pressure on other screens. Competition takes place through those exchanges rather than sharing the same physical level.

cards.heading: Coins and time keep a run alive
cards.text: Knowing the courses helps players reach hidden coins and avoid hazards. Coins can be spent on the item roulette, while enemy defeats replenish time. Extra enemies arriving from rivals can alter a section that would otherwise be easy to anticipate.

cards.heading: The end of the anniversary service
cards.text: The service ended with the anniversary celebration in March 2021. Its official matches depended on active servers and other participants. Recordings preserve examples of play after the service?s closure.
